market_context.summary: A two-speed tape, and the split is the rate. QQQ (747.46) and SPY (773.38) closed within 1% of their 120-day highs — QQQ ran +6.1% in four sessions — while every rate-sensitive sleeve made new lows: XLU 40.53 sits AT its 120-day low of 40.45 (-15.0% off the high), KRE -9.1%, IYR -8.8%, TLT 81.75 and -6.9% off its high. The driver is the long end: a 4.96% 10y against a 3.88% effective funds rate is +108bp of term premium with a +0.25 2s10s — a fiscal-supply tape, not a growth scare. Yesterday's single-stock action was almost entirely Meta's Muse launch: the market sold everything it decided depends on consumer inertia (SCHW -6%, ALL -5.5%, JPM/WFC -3%+, BKNG -3.9%, EXPE -3.7%, S&P Financials -2%), and the counter-catalyst landed this morning — Amazon has blocked Muse from its store for accessing it without authorisation. The useful work was separating the names that deserved the selloff (SCHW's cash-sorting risk, the OTAs) from those that did not: the tape had already priced principal-vs-agent correctly the same session, buying MAR +1.6% and DAL +1.7% while selling ABNB -3.0%. With SPY 0.8% off its high this is a rotation, not a risk-off, and a rotation can reverse on one soft CPI.

data_quality_notes:
RESEARCH RAN TO COMPLETION — notes.md carries a RESEARCH COMPLETE block (06:30 ET, amended, superseding an earlier one whose stamp had run ahead of the wall clock), so `truncated` is false and nothing here is reconstructed from fragments. 9 unique candidates from 10 captured lines; RCL appears twice and the second, re-levelled line supersedes the first.

SKEW, AND WHY: seven of nine recommendations are position management, not new risk. Only ALL and RCL are new positions, and only RCL is actionable at the market today (ALL carries wait:true — the first tranche is at 217.00, 5.4% below the last close). That is what the day actually offered against a book carrying 17 open positions and 12 awaiting-entry orders, several of them stale. Nothing intraday, no futures, no crypto and no event contract cleared the bar, each for a stated reason: CTAS and PAYX report within two hours with no fundamental edge on either; event contracts are unpriceable (below); bitcoin is 0.79% off its high after +13.5% in four sessions via IBIT, so there is nothing to short and nothing worth chasing, and the index-futures lane needs an index level that could not be fetched. A third new idea was explicitly declined rather than padded — the cross-sector de-rating screen produced UNH as the one genuine long-term candidate and it was carried to tomorrow because a half-researched mega-cap thesis is the failure mode, not the fix.

RATIOS: only two ideas are directional trades with a downside level; the other seven are exits, trims or withdrawals and carry no reward-to-risk by construction. Both were recomputed here from the final levels. RCL: entry 237.00, stop 220.00, target 272.00 = 2.06 against a 2.0 swing floor, stop 2.04 ATR against a 2.0 stock floor, break-even hit rate 32.7% against a claimed 40% (7.3 points of edge). FLAGGING IT HONESTLY: 2.06 is barely above the floor, and the entry was explicitly solved backwards from it — the pre-market had moved 234.89 to 238.85 before the open, and rather than nudge the target the research solved (272-E)/(E-220) >= 2.0 for E <= 237.33 and set 237.00. That is the better of the two ways to respond, but it is still fitting a level to the floor and the reader should size it as such. The idea carries its own kill switch: above 239.50 it is to be SKIPPED, not re-levelled. ALL: entry 215.00, bear case 195.00, target 272.00 = 2.85 against a 2.5 long-term floor, break-even 26.0% against a claimed 45% — 19.0 points of edge, just under the 20-point line where a claim is called large. The evidence that would actually carry that number — Allstate's historical rate-filing approval rates — was NOT researched.

CONVICTION: every score equals the number of distinct evidence kinds listed, except RCL, which lists four kinds (supporting a 5) and is published at 4 deliberately. It is a knife catch at a 200-day low and is sized 2% speculative; inflating the score to match the evidence count would be the wrong direction of error on this report's record.

WHAT COULD NOT BE CHECKED:
- Index, volatility, FX and commodity levels. Yahoo returned HTTP 429 for every one (^GSPC, ^NDX, ^DJI, ^RUT, ^VIX, ES=F, NQ=F, DX-Y.NYB, ^TNX, GC=F, CL=F); Finnhub refuses indices; stooq 404s on ^-symbols; no AlphaVantage key. The regime read is assembled from sector ETF history instead, and no index or VIX number appears anywhere in this report.
- Options-implied moves. Yahoo's options endpoint returns HTTP 401. NO target in this report was checked against what the options market prices, RCL's included.
- Short interest and days-to-cover. api.nasdaq.com `short` timed out (20s) on every symbol. No crowding read on any name.
- Event contracts. Kalshi returns count 0 for exact queries and unpriced multi-leg tickers for loose ones, so the three awaiting-entry KXFEDDECISION-* contracts could not be marked and no event idea was published.
- THE EARNINGS CALENDAR IS INCOMPLETE. Finnhub omitted General Mills, which reports before the open TODAY and is the direct read-across for the open CAG position — it was found from a pre-market story, not from the data source this run is built on. Treat the calendar as a floor, not a list. CCL's date is also contested between sources, which is why no CCL trade was published.
- RCL pro-forma leverage and covenants. The 8-K discloses neither. Partly addressed via the August 424B5, but the post-deal balance sheet is unverified and it is the open question in key_risk.
- Boise Cascade's +4.4% move on 09-22: no catalyst identifiable in the sources checked, so none was written.

PRICES: equity quotes re-fetched at synthesis returned the 2026-09-22 regular-session close for every symbol (session 'pre', age ~871 minutes) — that is a closed market, not stale data. Where a real-time pre-market read existed it is carried in last_price_asof; RCL's last_price is the 06:28 ET pre-market print of 238.85 because that idea's entry zone depends on it. GLD and EEM pre-market depth failed, and ALL's pre-market quote was ignored as noise on a 9.9% spread.

SOURCES THAT FAILED: query1/query2.finance.yahoo.com (429 on chart endpoints, 401 on options), Finnhub quote for indices (subscription required), stooq (404 on ^-prefixed symbols), api.nasdaq.com `short` for all symbols and `depth` for GLD/EEM (timeouts), Kalshi events (no matches), bloomberg.com (403), nasdaq.com market-activity earnings page (60s timeout). SOURCES THAT WORKED: api.nasdaq.com historical and depth, Finnhub (quotes, earnings calendar, profiles, analysts, insiders), SEC EDGAR (three primary documents read today — the RCL 8-K, the RCL 424B5 and the Allstate Exhibit 99), FRED, CoinGecko.

TRACK RECORD CONTEXT: 7 closed of 36 tracked is well under the ~15 needed to mean anything, so the 1/7 target rate is noise and is not being over-fit. What is not noise is the structural point the book surfaced today: several open longs (NKE, LULU, LCII, BCC, PFE) carry no stop and targets 50-75% away. NKE is being closed because a dated binary event forced the issue; the rest are on the watchlist as a book-structure problem.

RED TEAM (phase 2c) — cut 1 of 9, downgraded 1, left 7 management calls standing.

CUT RCL, the only new position that was actionable at the market today. The 8-K is real and says
exactly what the thesis quotes — verified against the filing — but it was not news. CNBC published
"Royal Caribbean nears $3 billion deal to take 50% equity stake in Sandals" on 2026-09-22, the same
session the stock fell 6.1%, so the market sold with the 50%/$3.0bn structure already in front of it.
The research read only the investing.com write-up of the FT piece ("majority stake", ">$6bn valuation")
and inferred the tape had feared something larger; it had not. Being right about the filing and early
to it are different things, and this was neither. The filing also confirms the objection rather than
retiring it — ~$3.0bn of new committed debt for a 50/50 land-resort JV — while the evidence item filed
as `counter_argument_answered` (the August $1.25bn 424B5) establishes only that RCL can refinance,
which is a different question. Full reasoning is on the watchlist entry.

DOWNGRADED ALL from conviction 4 to 3 and win_probability from 0.45 to 0.33. Two reasons, neither of
which kills the idea. First, the report itself states the 45% was unsupported — Allstate's historical
rate-filing approval rates, the one mechanism that would carry a 19-point edge over a 26% break-even,
were not researched — so the number is now set where the evidence actually reaches (+0.27R rather than
+0.73R). Second, ALL's 5.5% fall on 09-22 was a group move: Progressive, Primerica and Trupanion fell
with it as the market marked down severe-weather-exposed personal lines. The thesis reads the 17.2%
de-rating as a single-name overreaction of about 11x; the report's own counter-argument computes that
capitalising $1.1bn/yr at 12x reproduces the decline almost exactly, and the group move is evidence for
the counter-argument. Both are now recorded in `key_risk` and `counter_argument`. The staged 217/210/202
entry, 6.3% below the market and explicitly `wait: true`, is what keeps it publishable.

CUT NOTHING ELSE, and that is a finding rather than a pass. Seven of the eight survivors are position
management — a stop honoured (DVN), a stop finally raised on the book's only winner (EEM), two
contradictory GLD orders reconciled, two resting bids withdrawn after the move they were waiting for
happened without them (SNX, MU), and two exits ahead of dated events (CAG into this morning's General
Mills print, NKE into 10-01). Each carries a counter-argument that names what doing it costs, and none
of them widens a stop or nudges a target. There is nothing here to manufacture an objection about.

RANKING CHANGED. With RCL gone the report contains no new position that is actionable at today's open,
so the ranks now run by what has a deadline today: CAG must be halved before 09:30 ET, DVN exits at the
open, EEM's stop and GLD's order conflict are today's work. ALL is rank 5 because it is a limit order
6.3% below the market, not because it is the weakest idea.

FACTS THE RED TEAM VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY: the RCL 8-K (50% / ~$3.0bn / Morgan Stanley committed debt /
early-2027 close, no earnout); the Allstate Exhibit 99 ($748m pre-tax, $591m after-tax, 21 events, ~50%
one wind-and-hail event, $1.43bn/$1.13bn July-August, 216m policies — and confirmed it says nothing
about rate filings, which is why the win probability came down); General Mills reporting this morning
with Q&A at 8:00am CT; SNX 2026-09-24 bmo; and NIKE's own announcement of 2026-10-01 after the close.

TWO VALIDATOR ARTIFACTS THE READER SHOULD NOT ACT ON. The report shows 9 of 9 ideas failing, and most
of that is mechanical. (a) Every idea carries a `sources` FAIL for a 404 on
`api.nasdaq.com/api/quote/<SYM>/historical`. `check_sources` sends a bare HEAD; that endpoint needs
query parameters and 404s without them. The data behind it was genuinely fetched. It is a citation-
hygiene defect — an unparameterised API root is not a citable URL — not a hallucinated source, and not
grounds to cut anything. (b) The wide-spread FAILs on ALL (9.93%), CAG (12.54%), SNX (5.01%) and DVN
(4.09%) are pre-market quotes on large caps, ALL's being bid 228.00 against a 251.83 ask on a $58bn name
with $416m of daily volume. They are not the spread anyone trades at 09:30. Separately, the
`direction_consistency` / `risk_reward` / `stop_distance` failures on the seven management calls are the
validator scoring an exit as if it were an entry: a trade being closed has no target by construction.
The one contested date left standing: Finnhub's calendar carries NKE at 2026-09-28, against 2026-10-01
after the close in NIKE's own 2026-08-28 announcement. The primary source governs, but if the position
is still open, treat the earlier date as the deadline and not the later one.

watchlist.note: Red team cut this. The thesis was that the 2026-09-23 8-K disclosed something 'materially smaller' than the FT report that took the stock down 6.1% on 09-22, so the 8-K was a repricing catalyst. It was not new information: CNBC published 'Royal Caribbean nears $3 billion deal to take 50% equity stake in Sandals' on 2026-09-22 (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/22/royal-caribbean-sandals.html), the same session the stock fell. The market had the 50%/$3.0bn structure in front of it and sold anyway, so the 8-K confirms the tape rather than contradicting it and there is no edge to be early to. Second, the 8-K confirms the worry instead of answering it: ~$3.0bn of cash funded by committed Morgan Stanley debt is new leverage for a 50/50 JV in land-based resorts, and the 'counter_argument_answered' evidence — the 2026-08-10 $1.25bn 424B5 — shows only that RCL can refinance floating-rate paper at a fixed rate, which is a different question from whether $3.0bn of incremental debt is well spent. That drops the genuine confirmations to two (primary_document, technical_level), since the fourth kind, 'positioning', was itself listed as evidence AGAINST the trade. With the catalyst gone what remains is a knife catch at a new 200-day low, closing at the low of a 3.7-ATR down day, 19.6% off its 08-25 high in a sector-wide de-rating, on a 2.06:1 ratio whose 237.00 entry the research states plainly was solved backwards out of the 2.0 floor, with a 2.04 ATR stop and a 40% win probability against a 32.7% break-even that nothing supports.
watchlist.trigger: pro-forma leverage and covenants disclosed (the 8-K gives neither), or the cruise complex stops making lower lows — a close back above the 263.00 20-day. Do not re-enter on the deal news itself; it is priced.
watchlist.demotion_reason: the catalyst was already public when the stock fell on it; the edge never existed
